paper_metadata.title: Optimizing Mutual Fund Portfolio Management through the Application of Advanced Soft Computing Techniques
paper_metadata.venue: 2024 Third International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Information and Communication Technologies (ICEEICT)

summary: Integrated quantum-inspired framework combining a Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA) for mutual-fund portfolio allocation with a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for performance prediction. Evaluated on a 10-firm private-valuation dataset (Open AI, Chainalysis, Lacework, RAMP, Fireblocks, Dapper, Falconx, Labs/Consensys, Upgrade, iCapital Network) using actual vs predicted returns. Reports mean MAPE 5.45% for the QEA+QNN framework vs 5.68% for the traditional-methods baseline (Table I). Purely classical Python simulation; no gate-based QPU, simulator, qubit counts, circuit depth, or noise model reported.

experiments.description: QEA+QNN integrated framework for mutual-fund portfolio management: QEA optimizes portfolio allocation via quantum-inspired evolutionary operators (selection, crossover, mutation on qubit-encoded individuals); QNN predicts portfolio returns per firm using quantum-inspired gates on historical financial attributes (growth %, total funding, valuation, revenue, growth rates). Compared against traditional portfolio prediction methods on a 10-firm dataset. MAPE is the headline metric.

algorithm.variant: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA) for allocation + Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for return prediction; integrated feedback loop between QEA and QNN
algorithm.ansatz: Quantum-inspired qubit representation with superposition amplitudes used for population encoding in QEA; QNN uses quantum-inspired gate-style layers on normalized firm features. Specific circuit/ansatz structure not reported.
algorithm.optimizer: Evolutionary operators (selection, crossover, mutation) within QEA; QNN training method not specified in paper.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Firm-level financial attributes (growth %, total funding, valuation, revenue, growth rates, historical returns). Preprocessing: IQR outlier removal, min-max normalization to [0,1], mean/median imputation for missing values. Features fed to a quantum-inspired neural network; portfolio weights encoded as quantum-inspired individuals in the QEA.
problem_formulation.constraints: Portfolio allocation constraints (diversification, investor risk tolerance) mentioned qualitatively; not formalized numerically.

problem_instance.dataset_name: Firm-level private company valuations and returns (10 firms)

dataset_specification.description: 10 companies: Open AI, Chainalysis, Lacework, RAMP, Fireblocks, Dapper, Falconx, Labs/Consensys, Upgrade, iCapital Network. Features include growth %, total funding, valuation, revenue, growth rates, historical returns. Actual returns per firm range 3.8%-7.3% (Table I). Industry valuations (Fig. 2) cover transport (5.7), AI (4.311), DeliveryTech (4.1), fintech (3.842), gaming (3.5), etc.
dataset_specification.source: Firm-level financial data (sources not cited in detail)

results.notes: Table I, 'Proposed Integrated Framework' column. Mean absolute percentage error across 10 firms on predicted vs actual returns.
